analyticalQuestion: After the exact normalization A^4 G4/(A^2 G2)=-(epsilon^2/L^2)R_{L,M,m}, does the complete quartic target coefficient show growth with the number M of coherent outputs on the archived deterministic scan?
supportedClaim: Every one of the 461 distinct archived ratios is positive, so every observed quartic target opposes the quadratic target. The largest observed ratio is 0.0013286562612066827, and the edge-target families show no numerical growth with M up to the scanned endpoint M=8192. These are finite observations, not all-index positivity or boundedness theorems.

variants: 416 complete target-profile observations in four parameter families on a logarithmic response scale
48 distinct edge-target observations across dyadic scaling families
one directly annotated observed maximum and one high-precision reliability statement
chartContract.takeaway: The archived quartic target is always opposite in phase to the quadratic target, remains small after L^-2 normalization, and exhibits no observed M-growth; the uniform theorem is still open.
chartContract.dataSufficiency: The certificate contains 464 evaluations including three duplicates, 461 distinct triples, 49 distinct parameter pairs, and 7,494,536,238 ordered quartic paths. Panel (a) displays all 416 targets in four representative families. Panel (b) displays all 48 distinct baseline and extended edge pairs.

computation.configuration: three deterministic long-double scan families: 30 baseline edge pairs, 18 extended edge pairs through M=8192, and 416 individual targets in four complete families; the observed maximum was recomputed at 60 decimal digits
computation.precision: C++ long double with compensated signed and absolute sums, stable confluent divided differences, and an independent mpmath 60-decimal recomputation at the observed maximum
computation.solver: complete ordered enumeration of every quartic target path A+B-C=Q, with analytic repeated-rate derivatives in the three-simplex heat kernel
